correctness.rationale: The established planar convex Cheeger equation |Omega_t ominus sB|=pi s^2 uniquely defines radius s=1/h; support functions imply for s<=t the erosion is P+(t-s)B, and otherwise P ominus(s-t)B. At s=t the residual is A-pi t^2, giving exact universal threshold. Steiner area yields s=(A+Lt+pi t^2)/(L+2pi t) above threshold. For u small, |P ominus uB|=A-Lu+Cu^2 by corner-triangle area, C=sum cot(alpha_i/2). The implicit subthreshold equation has derivative -(L+2pi T), so differentiable roots with b1=2pi T/D, b2=pi(4pi C T^2-L^2)/D^3; direct independent SymPy differentiation verified the boxed h second derivative jump. Exterior-angle Jensen yields C>pi and hence strict non-C2 behavior. The local inner area polynomial is used only before edge extinction.
residual_risks: No globally analytic subthreshold Cheeger profile is claimed; its inward polygon edges can disappear at later t.

value.rationale: The exact universal second-derivative defect, valid for every genuine convex polygon, detects the intrinsic corner functional C=sum cot(alpha_i/2) from physically natural disk-offset Cheeger response. Sharp regularity loss at a universal area-normalized scale extends known first-variation theory and supplies a shape-sensitivity benchmark. The bound and geometric object are motivated independently of finite numerical examples.
residual_risks: No global subthreshold closed form asserted, and the threshold itself is a known-theorem implication.

limitations: Plane convex polygon with genuine corners and Euclidean unit-disk offsets; t near positive threshold for analytic expansions.
C is not a full determination of individual angles; jump is one scalar angular invariant.
